newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber end mostly up in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber end mostly up in quiet market.

text.p: Rubber futures closed mostly higher on Monday in thin trade with lower Japanese prices partly weighing on market sentiment, dealers said.
"It was a soft and quiet market. Basically, nobody wanted to do anything today and the offtakes were fairly light," a local rubber trader said.
Another trader said the impact of profit-taking in Japan, where prices came down from early highs, knocked sentiment down.

"Higher prices in Japan could have lifted sentiment, but it came off and that weakened the local market," one trader said. Tokyo's new benchmark April contract shed 1.4 yen from its opening to settle at 139.8 while Kobe's new April contract closed at 140.0 yen after opening at 141.7.
At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 125.50 U.S. cents a kg from 125.75 cents.
December RSS1 was seen at 179.00-180.00 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.28) a kg from 179.00 cents.
December TSR20 was seen at 174.25-175.25 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.24) a kg against 174.25 cents.
